data.title: Understand a Project's Tech Stack
data.outcome: Identify a project's main technology layers and know what is responsible for changing, running, and deploying it.
intentExamples: I can't understand this project's tech stack
What's the relationship between React and Next.js?
I'm taking over an unfamiliar project

stages.title: Separate the page, server, and data layers
stages.action: Map the main layers of the current project from page to data.
stages.evidence: You can identify the layers a feature passes through.

lessons.title: Tech Stack
lessons.tagline: The set of languages, frameworks, data services, and tools used to build and run software

lessons.title: Frontend
lessons.tagline: The layer people directly see, click, and type into

lessons.title: Backend
lessons.tagline: The server-side part people usually cannot see that handles requests and data

lessons.title: Database
lessons.tagline: Store and find application data such as users, posts, and orders

stages.title: Identify the language and type rules
stages.action: Use configuration and file extensions to identify the main language.
stages.evidence: You know which files contain running code and which contain only types or configuration.

lessons.title: JavaScript
lessons.tagline: A programming language that makes a web page respond to actions and data

lessons.title: TypeScript
lessons.tagline: A language that checks written code for mismatched names and value types before it runs

stages.title: Understand the project structure the framework provides
stages.action: Use dependencies and directories to identify the framework the project actually uses.
stages.evidence: You can find the page entry points, components, and server-side code.

lessons.title: React
lessons.tagline: A JavaScript library for building interactive interfaces from components and state

lessons.title: Next.js
lessons.tagline: A React framework for building full websites and web applications

lessons.title: Vue
lessons.tagline: A JavaScript framework for building interactive interfaces with templates and components

stages.title: Find where styling and components come from
stages.action: Check the CSS and component approach the project actually uses.
stages.evidence: You will not introduce a duplicate styling system while making changes.

lessons.title: Tailwind CSS
lessons.tagline: A utility-first CSS framework that styles elements through small class names

lessons.title: shadcn/ui
lessons.tagline: A collection of editable UI component code that you add to a React project
